pr.title: Add support for local settings in configuration editing
pr.body:
Fixes #40233

reviews.body:
## Pull Request Overview

This PR adds support for local settings files (`settings.local.json`) in VS Code's configuration system. Local settings take precedence over workspace and user settings, providing developers with a way to override configurations without affecting shared workspace settings.

Key changes include:
- Added support for `settings.local.json` files in workspace folders
- Implemented proper precedence where local settings override workspace and user settings
- Added comprehensive test coverage for local settings functionality

### Reviewed Changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `src/vs/workbench/services/configuration/common/configuration.ts` | Defines constants for local settings file names and schema identifiers |
| `src/vs/workbench/services/configuration/browser/configurationService.ts` | Registers JSON schema for local settings validation |
| `src/vs/workbench/services/configuration/browser/configuration.ts` | Core implementation for loading, parsing, and merging local settings with other configuration sources |
| `src/vs/workbench/services/configuration/test/browser/configurationService.test.ts` | Comprehensive test suite covering local settings loading, precedence, and file operations |
| `extensions/configuration-editing/package.json` | Adds JSON schema association for `settings.local.json` files |
</details>
I think it is ready to go

Great. Could you refer me to the issue on Cursor? I'll plus 1 it :)

With more and more tools taking the "ignored `.local` config" approach, ~~I'm surprised this isn't getting more attention.~~ (it is getting lots of attention, the linked issue has 1300+ reactions and 250+ comments 🫨). I'd love to see some progress, so [I'll do my part](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5fb24e0-51e8-4e82-9778-812e7cf8e774).

I think there's a few considerations here, particularly relating to the UX of such a feature. I'm going to list a few questions I can think of, not because they all _need_ answers, but to point out that nothing is simple and this is typically why product teams say "not right now". Bike-shedding over naming is just one part of a larger discussion.

- How will users _know_ that a setting comes from `.local`? Could/should VSCode ...
  - display a new tab in the settings view for 'Local'?
  - show affordance in the "Settings (JSON)" view to show which takes precedence (such as strikethrough on lines in `.vscode/settings.json` that are also in `.vscode/settings.local.json`)? 
- What if someone doesn't have a `.gitignore` file? Could/should VSCode ...
  - suggest that the `.vscode/settings.local.json` file be commited?
  - suggest ignoring the file?
  - ignore the settings?
- What if the folder isn't a git repo at all?
  - _[same questions as above]_
- What about team requirements? Could/should VSCode ...
  - provide a way for `.local` settings to be ignored over workspace settings? (some teams require specific settings from an org/company level and committed settings are an easy way to enforce this)
- What about multi-root workspaces?

---

_P.S. @yordis, I love you for this. Good to see you outside of wasmcloud!_

@lachieh Some thoughts about your points  
_(To preface this, I try to assume a generic scm)_

>    * How will users _know_ that a setting comes from `.local`? Could/should VSCode ...
>      * display a new tab in the settings view for 'Local'?
>      * show affordance in the "Settings (JSON)" view to show which takes precedence (such as strikethrough on lines in `.vscode/settings.json` that are also in `.vscode/settings.local.json`)?

- Presumably the same as for User (`settings.json` in vscode's data dir) <-> Workspace (`.vscode/settings.json`) Settings
  - _So show a new tab in the settings view for `Workspace (Local)`_
  - _(This is assuming simple single root folder workspaces)_

>    * What if someone doesn't have a `.gitignore` file? Could/should VSCode ...
>      * suggest that the `.vscode/settings.local.json` file be commited?
>      * suggest ignoring the file?
>      * ignore the settings?

- I see several options:
  1. Don't do anything, assume that the user is smart enough to understand that they shouldn't commit the file
  2. Warn in the _source control_ panel, ie:
    - Render some warning with the filename
    - Warn when trying to stage the file (user might not want to _commit_ nor add the file to the `.gitignore`)
    - Warn when attempting to create a commit with the file
  3. Place a `.gitignore` in the `.vscode` folder that ignores `settings.local.json`
    - but that wouldn't be scm independent

>    * What if the folder isn't a git repo at all?
>      * _[same questions as above]_

- use the file like normal, no reason to have it randomly not work

>    * What about team requirements? Could/should VSCode ...
>      * provide a way for `.local` settings to be ignored over workspace settings? (some teams require specific settings from an org/company level and committed settings are an easy way to enforce this)

- `settings.local.json` is meant to be for settings that should not be committed, such as settings _with absolute paths_ / _that depend on machine specific things_

>    * What about multi-root workspaces?

- Works just like `.vscode/settings.json` (but takes precedence)
